private_lines.Kasia: You live in Kraków in a flat near the Vistula, and you work as a pharmacist in a busy shop on the main square. This week you are juggling late shifts with helping your younger sister choose a venue for her wedding in the spring.
private_lines.Michał: You live in Gdańsk in a two-room flat in Oliwa, and you work as a logistics planner for a shipping company near the port. This week you are sorting out paperwork for a flat you are about to buy and trying to get through a backlog of shipping schedules before the end of the month.

setting: You both live in Poland, Kasia in Kraków and Michał in Gdańsk, and you have been friends since secondary school in Tarnów, where you sat together in chemistry and still tease each other about it. You have kept in touch through a loose chat for years, mostly with birthday messages and the odd photo, and you know each other's families, jobs and the usual ups and downs. Your last exchange was about whether the bakery near the old station still does the poppy-seed rolls.

Kasia.knows: You know Michał is the one who always remembered everyone's birthdays and who once drove you to the airport at four in the morning. You know he moved to Gdańsk for work about six years ago and that he is still single as far as you can tell.
Kasia.texts: You message the chat now and then without being asked, and you usually write in lowercase with minimal punctuation, using a laughing emoji when something amuses you. Your messages are short, often a single line, though you write longer when you are catching up on news.
ex: ok the rolls are still there but they cost more now
did you get my voice note about the wedding dress
i am on a break so answer quickly
are you coming to the christmas market thing in december
that photo of your cat is the best thing i have seen all week

Michał.knows: You know Kasia is the one who kept the whole class group together after school and who is always planning something. You know she works as a pharmacist in Kraków and that she has a younger sister getting married soon.
Michał.texts: You reply to the chat when someone else starts a conversation, and you rarely send messages without a reason. You write in normal sentences with proper capitals and full stops, use an emoji only occasionally, and keep your messages to a line or two.
ex: Yes, the rolls are still there, I checked last week.
Sorry, I missed your voice note, I will listen later.
Good luck with the shifts, sounds exhausting.
I can make it to Kraków in December if the trains work.
Did you see the weather forecast for the weekend?

opener: Asks Michał whether he is still coming to the school reunion in March.
situation: Old school friends who live in different cities now.
